issues.legal_issue: An inconsistent local amendment to civil procedure ceases to operate upon commencement of the amending legislation even when the corresponding provision of the uniform code was not itself amended.
material_facts: A local amendment had deleted the provisions requiring a decree-holder to obtain express permission before bidding for or purchasing property in execution and allowing the sale to be set aside for purchase without permission.
The later amending legislation did not amend the corresponding rule, and the proceedings were governed by the Code as amended.
The statutory savings provisions did not preserve the local amendment at issue.
issues.conclusion: The inconsistent local amendment stood repealed, and the Code as amended governed the proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Section 97(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (Amendment) Act, 1976 repeals local amendments inconsistent with the principal Act as amended, whether or not the corresponding provision was itself amended. This is subject to section 97(2); section 97(3) applies the amended Code to the proceedings it covers. The purpose is to provide uniform procedural law until a later local amendment is validly made. The Court referred to the Law Commission's 54th Report on retaining the safeguard in Order 21 Rule 72. No earlier judicial decisions were relied on.

predicates.civil_proceeding_governed_by_code: The dispute proceeded in a civil court whose procedure was governed by the general civil procedure code.
predicates.local_procedure_inconsistent_with_unifor: A local procedural amendment differed from the procedure in the general code as amended.
predicates.no_saving_exception_applies: No applicable saving provision preserved the inconsistent local procedure.

issues.definition: When a civil proceeding is governed by the code, a conflicting local procedure ceases to apply unless a saving exception preserves it.

issues.legal_issue: A decree-holder's purchase of property at an execution sale without express court permission may be set aside when the applicable procedure retains that safeguard and an affected person applies.
material_facts: A decree-holder purchased property at a court sale without obtaining the executing court's express permission.
Before the sale was confirmed, the judgment-debtor applied to set it aside on that ground.
The local amendment that had removed the permission requirement and the remedy for an unauthorised purchase was inconsistent with the procedure governing the proceedings.
The executing court set aside the sale, and the District Judge affirmed that decision.
issues.conclusion: The sale was properly set aside, and the order affirming that result was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Order 21 Rule 72(1) of the Code requires a decree-holder to obtain the court's express permission to bid for or purchase property sold in execution. Under Order 21 Rule 72(3), the court may set aside a purchase made without permission on an application by the judgment-debtor or another person whose interests are affected. Section 97(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (Amendment) Act, 1976 caused the inconsistent local deletion of these safeguards to cease to operate. No earlier judicial decisions were relied on.

rule.if: execution_sale_challenge and decree_holder_bought_without_permission and affected_person_applied_to_set_aside and local_procedure_inconsistent_with_uniform_code

predicates.execution_sale_challenge: A party sought review of the result of a sale conducted by a court to enforce a decree.
predicates.decree_holder_bought_without_permission: The decree-holder purchased the property at the execution sale without express permission from the executing court.
predicates.affected_person_applied_to_set_aside: The judgment-debtor or another person whose interests were affected applied to set aside the sale.
predicates.local_procedure_inconsistent_with_unifor: A local procedural amendment had removed the general safeguards against a decree-holder's unauthorised purchase.

issues.definition: When an execution sale is challenged, the decree-holder bought without permission, an affected person applied to set the sale aside, and the local procedure removing that safeguard conflicts with the governing procedure, the sale is set aside.

issues.legal_issue: An application to set aside an execution sale should not be rejected as time-barred where uncertainty about the applicable procedure existed and the lower courts did not reject it on limitation grounds.
material_facts: The judgment-debtor's application relying on the permission requirement was made after the initial application to set aside the sale, and the delay was condoned.
The decree-holder argued before the Supreme Court that the application was time-barred.
The applicability of the permission requirement in the jurisdiction had been uncertain.
Neither the High Court nor the subordinate courts had rejected the application on limitation grounds.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to reject the application as time-barred.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered it unjust to entertain the limitation objection in the circumstances, given the uncertainty over whether the procedural safeguard applied and the fact that the courts below had not rejected the application on that ground. No statutory limitation provision or earlier judicial decision was relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: appellate_review_of_execution_sale_order and applicability_of_sale_safeguard_was_uncertain and lower_courts_did_not_reject_on_limitation and application_delay_was_condoned

predicates.appellate_review_of_execution_sale_order: An appellate court reviewed a dispute concerning an application to set aside a court execution sale.
predicates.applicability_of_sale_safeguard_was_unce: The parties and courts faced uncertainty about whether the procedural safeguard against an unauthorised decree-holder purchase applied.
predicates.lower_courts_did_not_reject_on_limitatio: The courts below did not dismiss the application on the ground that it was filed too late.
predicates.application_delay_was_condoned: The delay in making the application was accepted by the court.

issues.definition: In appellate review, when the safeguard's applicability was uncertain, the lower courts did not reject the application as late, and its delay was condoned, the application is not rejected as time-barred.
